_comment: Ambiguous events: identical or near-identical appearances that can lead to very different outcomes depending on player knowledge and choices. ~20% of new pool. These events teach players to read subtle distinctions, and reward prior memory.

events.title: Glowing Growth
events.description: Deep in a cave alcove you notice a soft blue-green glow on the wall. A cluster of small mushroom-like growths coats the rock, each one faintly luminescent. They're unlike anything you've seen before.

cues.description: Small mushroom-like growths glowing faint blue-green on rock
Faintly musty — not unpleasant
No insects or animals near the growth despite nearby food sources

choices.text: The glow looks interesting — taste one

outcome.description: Bioluminescent doesn't mean safe. Your mouth numbs within minutes and your vision blurs by the hour. Whatever these were, they were not food.

memory_reward.title: Glowing Cave Fungus
memory_reward.description: Bioluminescent blue-green cave fungus. Toxic. Mouth numbing, vision disturbance. Glow is not a sign of safety — quite the opposite.
hidden_traits: no insects near it = another warning sign

cue_tags.description: blue-green glow in cave

choices.text: Observe it carefully without touching — notice anything around it?

outcome.description: You look more carefully. No insects. No animal droppings nearby despite a rich environment. Nothing is eating this. That tells you something.

memory_reward.title: Glowing Cave Fungus
memory_reward.description: Bioluminescent cave fungus — nothing eats it. No insects nearby despite rich habitat. If nothing wants to eat it, there's a reason. Avoid.
hidden_traits: some glowing fungi are safe — requires specific identification

cue_tags.description: blue-green glow on cave wall
no insects or droppings near the growth

choices.text: Check what you know — bioluminescence in fungi is usually a warning

outcome.description: You recall the pattern: no insects, no animal sign near it. Bioluminescent cave fungi in your experience are toxic. You mark the location and move on, wiser.

memory_reward.title: Glowing Cave Fungus (Confirmed)
memory_reward.description: Bioluminescent cave fungus confirmed toxic by prior experience. Glow + no insects = reliable toxicity indicator in cave fungi.

cue_tags.description: blue-green bioluminescent growth, no insects near

events.title: Something Dead on the Path
events.description: A deer carcass lies across the trail, partially eaten. The ribcage is open. Flies buzz. Whether this is old or fresh is hard to say from here — there's no visible predator.

cues.description: Deer carcass with open ribcage, partially consumed
Strong decay smell — flies buzzing heavily
Claw marks on the flank larger than a wolf's

choices.text: Take a closer look — check if the kill is fresh

outcome.description: Close up, the wounds are dried and the smell is several days old. Old kill — the predator is long gone. But you're right beside the carcass when a different bear arrives to reclaim it.

memory_reward.title: Fresh Kill Site
memory_reward.description: A predator kill site is a feeding ground — the predator returns. Old or new, avoid close approach. Claw size indicates the predator.
hidden_traits: ravens circling above a spot = fresh kill below

cue_tags.description: heavy decay smell around carcass
claw marks on flank, size indicates predator

choices.text: Wide detour — you don't know who made this kill

outcome.description: Smart instinct. From higher ground you see a large brown shape return to the kill site below. You were never on its radar.

memory_reward.title: Predator Kill — Avoid
memory_reward.description: Any carcass on a trail is a predator feeding site — the predator will return. Wide detour regardless of how old the kill appears.

cue_tags.description: decay smell from partially eaten carcass

events.title: Tracks in the Mud
events.description: Fresh prints in a muddy section of trail. Large, four-toed, with a wide pad. They're bigger than a dog's but the shape is ambiguous — could be wolf, could be something else. The prints are today's.

cues.description: Large four-toed prints with wide pad, fresh mud — today's
Stride length suggests a fast, efficient gait

choices.text: Follow the tracks — find out what's ahead

outcome.description: The tracks lead to a clearing. At the far edge, a wolf watches from the treeline. It's alone and the light is midday — it turns and vanishes. Your curiosity paid off with useful information.

memory_reward.title: Wolf Track Reading
memory_reward.description: Large four-toed prints, wide pad, efficient stride = wolf. Following tracks safely in daylight gave advance warning of the animal's range.
hidden_traits: claw marks visible in wolf prints unlike dog prints

cue_tags.description: four-toed wide-pad print, claw marks visible

choices.text: Note them and move on — fresh tracks mean the animal is close

outcome.description: You give the area a wide berth. You hear movement in the treeline but nothing approaches. Awareness kept you clear.

memory_reward.title: Animal Tracks — Stay Alert
memory_reward.description: Fresh tracks = the animal is close. Identify what you can and increase alertness. Wide pad four-toed = likely wolf.

cue_tags.description: fresh four-toed prints in mud

events.title: Fog on the High Path
events.description: The trail climbs into thick fog. Visibility drops to a few metres. You know the path bends somewhere ahead — but in the fog you can't see where. You can hear wind on your left, which means open air.

cues.description: Thick fog — visibility only a few metres
Wind sound louder on your left, suggesting open air or drop
Ground narrows slightly underfoot

choices.text: Keep your current pace — stay on the path

outcome.description: The path bends right but the fog hides the turn completely. You step off the edge onto loose scree. You slide several metres before stopping against a rock outcrop, badly shaken.

memory_reward.title: Fog on High Paths
memory_reward.description: Fog on narrow high paths is dangerous. Wind on one side = open air or drop nearby. Slow to a shuffle in fog near cliff edges — every step must be tested first.
hidden_traits: tap the ground ahead with a stick before stepping in fog near cliffs

cue_tags.description: wind louder on one side in fog
narrowing ground underfoot in fog

choices.text: Stop and wait for the fog to thin before continuing

outcome.description: Twenty minutes later the fog lifts enough to reveal the path clearly. Directly ahead, the trail bends sharply right — and the left side is a ten-metre drop onto rocks. The wait was everything.

memory_reward.title: Wait Out Fog Near Cliffs
memory_reward.description: In fog on high paths, wind on one side = cliff edge possible. Wait for visibility before moving. The ten minutes saved is not worth the risk of the ten-metre drop.

cue_tags.description: wind louder on one side in heavy fog on high path

events.title: Dark Pool in the Hollow
events.description: A shaded hollow holds a perfectly still pool. The water is very dark from tannins but otherwise clear — you can see leaves on the bottom. No visible algae. No smell. You're very thirsty.

cues.description: Dark brown-tinted still water — tannins from leaves
Leaves clearly visible on pool bottom, no green film
No smell at all — clean air around the pool

choices.text: Drink it — dark from tannins is not the same as contaminated

outcome.description: You're right. Tannin-dark water is common in forested hollows and is safe when clear and odourless. The taste is slightly astringent but you feel no ill effect.

memory_reward.title: Tannin Pool
memory_reward.description: Dark brown water in forest hollows is from leaf tannins — not contamination. Safe to drink if: clear, odourless, visible bottom, no algae film.
hidden_traits: green or milky still water is contaminated — dark-clear is fine

cue_tags.description: dark clear water, visible bottom, no film
completely odourless

choices.text: Don't risk it — still water is always suspect

outcome.description: You go on thirsty. The pool was probably fine — tannin-dark forest water often is — but without knowing for sure, you made the safer choice.

memory_reward.title: Tannin Pool Uncertainty
memory_reward.description: Dark still forest pool. Avoided it — not sure if safe. Dark colour alone is not always a danger sign in tannin-rich forest hollows.

events.title: Birds Exploding From the Trees
events.description: A mass of birds bursts from the treetops ahead of you without visible cause — all at once, all in the same direction. The forest goes quiet afterward. Something disturbed them that you didn't see.

cues.description: Sudden mass bird flush from treetops ahead
Alarm calls and wingbeats, then sudden silence

choices.text: Stop and watch — something caused that flush

outcome.description: You freeze. Thirty seconds later a large brown shape crosses the trail fifty metres ahead — a bear, unhurried. It vanishes without seeing you. The birds gave you a warning you acted on.

memory_reward.title: Bird Flush = Predator Ahead
memory_reward.description: Sudden mass bird flush from forest treetops = large animal disturbed them nearby. Stop and wait before continuing — the animal is usually between you and where the birds went.
hidden_traits: birds flush from below upward when alarmed by ground predator

cue_tags.description: mass sudden bird flush from canopy ahead
alarm calls then abrupt silence

choices.text: Keep moving — birds flush all the time

outcome.description: You walk straight into the bear's path. The encounter is brief and bad. You get away but not without damage. The birds were telling you something and you didn't listen.

memory_reward.title: Ignored Bird Flush Warning
memory_reward.description: A sudden mass bird flush from treetops was a predator warning. Ignored it, walked into the animal's path. Stop when birds flush suddenly — they know the forest.

cue_tags.description: sudden mass bird flush ahead

events.title: Cave with Echoing Sounds
events.description: You're considering sheltering in a promising cave when you hear sounds from inside. Rhythmic, regular. Could be dripping water. Could be breathing. The entrance is dark and you can't see far.

cues.description: Rhythmic, regular sound from inside the cave — dripping or breathing
Cool air from inside — no strong animal smell, but some earthiness
Darkness inside — nothing visible beyond a few metres

choices.text: Go in slowly — it's probably just dripping water

outcome.description: The sound is not water. A large shape shifts at the back of the cave. You back out fast but not without being swatted — something large was sleeping there.

memory_reward.title: Occupied Cave — Don't Enter
memory_reward.description: Rhythmic sounds from inside a cave could be an animal at rest. Smell check first — animal scent means occupied. Do not enter a cave you cannot see into fully.
hidden_traits: bears and big cats den in caves with multiple entry points

cue_tags.description: rhythmic regular sound from cave interior
animal musk from cave entrance

choices.text: Make noise at the entrance first — if something is inside, let it know you're there

outcome.description: You clap and shout. Movement inside — something large heads deeper in through a second exit you hadn't seen. You wait, then enter to find an empty warm alcove. The previous occupant relocated.

memory_reward.title: Cave Entry Protocol
memory_reward.description: Before entering a dark cave with sounds, make noise at the entrance. Animals prefer to avoid confrontation — give them the chance to leave through another exit.
hidden_traits: most caves used by animals have more than one exit

cue_tags.description: sounds from cave interior

events.title: Bones in a Clearing
events.description: In a small clearing you find a loose scatter of bones — large ones, from a deer or similar animal. Some are gnawed. The clearing has no recent animal smell, but the bones look relatively clean.

cues.description: Scattered large bones, gnawed, relatively clean and dry
Very faint old decay smell — mostly gone
No tracks in the clearing, no fresh sign

choices.text: Examine the bones — determine how old and what animal made this kill

outcome.description: The bones are dry and bleached — months old at least. The gnaw marks match a bear's teeth pattern. No fresh sign in the clearing. This site is long abandoned. You camp near here safely.

memory_reward.title: Reading Kill Site Age
memory_reward.description: Dry bleached bones = old kill, months minimum. Fresh kills have wet bones and strong smell. Dry bones + no tracks + no smell = abandoned site, likely safe.
traits: safe to camp near old kills
hidden_traits: fresh kill has red-brown staining and wet marrow visible

cue_tags.description: dry bleached gnawed bones
no significant smell remaining near the bones

choices.text: Leave the area — bone scatters mean predator territory

outcome.description: A cautious response. The site was old and abandoned, so you missed a decent camping spot — but you also missed nothing dangerous.

memory_reward.title: Bone Scatter — Uncertain
memory_reward.description: Found a bone scatter and left without reading the signs. Could have been old and safe. Learning to age kill sites removes unnecessary detours.

events.title: Dead Circle in the Forest
events.description: You notice a roughly circular patch of dead and dying plants — about three metres across. Everything inside is wilted and yellow. The surrounding trees are healthy. There is no obvious reason for it.

cues.description: Circular dead plant patch, 3m across — surrounding vegetation healthy
Faint sour or sulphur smell when you approach the edge

choices.text: Walk through it — probably just a shaded or dry patch

outcome.description: Within the circle you feel lightheaded and your eyes water. You walk out quickly but the headache lasts hours. A natural CO2 or sulphur vent — invisible and heavier than air, pooling at ground level.

memory_reward.title: Ground Gas Vent
memory_reward.description: Circular dead plant patches in otherwise healthy forest = possible ground gas vent. CO2 and sulphur are heavier than air and kill plants first. Never walk through.
hidden_traits: animals collapse and die inside gas vents — avoid any with animal bones

cue_tags.description: circular dead plant patch in healthy forest
sour or sulphur smell at the patch edge

choices.text: Approach the edge only — smell the air before going in

outcome.description: At the edge you catch a faint sulphur note. You back away and circle around it widely. Something is venting from underground — the plants are showing you what the air can't.

memory_reward.title: Dead Plant Circle — Smell Test
memory_reward.description: Circular dead plant patches in healthy forest are a warning. Smell the edge before entering — sulphur or sour smell = ground gas vent. Plants are the early warning system.
traits: circular dead patch = gas vent possible

cue_tags.description: circular dead zone in healthy vegetation
sulphur smell at the perimeter
